title: Regional Quiescence: SLO-Gated Alert Throttle and Automated Runbook Orchestration
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: During recent multi-region degradation drills we saw a cascade of low-value alerts that drowned the on-call team while a handful of resources were the true failure points. Existing SLO-linked paging is binary; once an alert fires for a route it pages immediately. Scope: Implement an SLO-driven alert throttling layer that enables regional quiescence windows, probabilistic dampening, and automated runbook orchestration tied to stateful circuit-breaker signals and load-shedding events. The feature should live in the alert orchestration service and integrate with PagerDuty, Console alert rules, and our routing layer so that: 1) noisy, correlated alerts can be suppressed for a short, observable quiescence period; 2) alerts escalate if SLOs repeatedly breach during quiescence; 3) circuit-breaker openings and graceful load-shedding can trigger a targeted runbook automation that attempts self-remediation before paging; 4) precise audit logs and revert actions are recorded for post-incident analysis. Goals: reduce page noise by 40% for multi-region transient faults, reduce mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for high-impact degradations by 25%, and provide deterministic, testable runbook automation for standard failover patterns.
acceptance_criteria: Configurable SLO-gated throttle that suppresses low-importance alerts for a configurable quiescence window (default 90s) and then escalates if the SLO remains violated
Circuit-breaker emits a canonical 'quiescence_reason' event consumed by alert orchestrator and runbook runner

Automated runbook tasks for the three common failure vectors (network partition between regions, autoscaler thrash, model serving OOM) that can perform safe remediations and record actions to audit logs
Observable dashboard: per-route throttle rate, suppressed alerts, SLO state transitions, and runbook outcomes in Console/Grafana
End-to-end e2e test harness + chaos experiment reproducing a transient spike that demonstrates suppression then escalation semantics
Playbook in Console docs with clear operator steps when automatic remediation fails
implementation_notes: Design: introduce 'alert_orchestrator' microservice that subscribes to SLO streams (slo-events), circuit-breaker state changes (cb-events), and metric anomalies; maintain per-route state with an in-memory LRU plus durable journal for auditability.

Throttling algorithm: SLO-gated probabilistic dampening. For a route r, when SLO breach is detected, start quiescence timer t_q; during t_q, convert immediate pages to probability p(t) = min(1, alpha * elapsed/t_q) for non-critical alerts. Critical alerts bypass dampening.

Stateful circuit breaker integration: when cb opens due to error_pct or latency, issue a 'quiescence_reason' tag with metadata {region, reason, scored_impact} consumed by orchestrator. Circuit breaker will also expose 'forced_open' metadata for manual ops.

Runbook runner: extend our existing runbook service to support programmatic steps (API calls to router, autoscaler, and runtime control plane), dry-run mode, and safety checks. Each automated step must include revert action recorded in audit log.

Routing interaction: orchestrator can request targeted regional failover (golden routes) using smart routing API; this request should incrementally route 10/30/100% and observe SLO delta before escalating.

Fallback: if orchestrator detects rapid re-escalation (more than N reopens within T minutes), immediately escalate to on-call with full context bundle and disable further throttling for that route for the duration of incident.

Testing: build a synthetic spike harness in chaos-suite that simulates multi-region network degradation, validate suppressed pages, and assert that automated runbook reduces error rate by >30% before paging.
Metrics to emit: suppressed_alert_count, throttle_rate, quiescence_sessions, runbook_invocations, runbook_success_rate, cb_open_count, regional_failover_executions
runbook_snippet: Trigger: cb-open with scored_impact>=0.2 or slo-breach for 3 consecutive 1m buckets
Step 1 (automated): attempt golden-route partial shift (10% traffic) to adjacent region via routing API; wait 30s and observe lat_p50/p95 and error rate
Step 2 (automated): if error rate improves >15%, increment to 30% and continue monitoring; if not, run autoscaler policy 'scale-to-safe' on affected pool
Step 3 (automated): if autoscaler fails or OOM detected, restart model-serving task with 'graceful-drain' annotation; log action and start a revert timer
Step 4 (manual): if thresholds continue to breach after two iterations, page L2 with context bundle and recommended remediation steps
Revert: each automated action has a one-click revert link that undoes routing change and restarts drain-excluded tasks back to previous state
